newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends touch lower. [CORRECTED 12:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends touch lower. [CORRECTED 12:45 GMT]

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee ended a touch lower after moving in a tight range determined by import covering and market sentiment, dealers said.
(Corrects headline and text to show rupee fell slightly and did not end stronger against the dollar.)
The rupee closed at 57.25 to the dollar, after opening at 57.23. The currency closed at 57.20 on Wednesday.
"Import covering supported the bottom, while market sentiment that the Central Bank is keen to maintain overall rates low, capped the top," said a Hatton National Bank dealer.
The Central Bank this week cut its overnight repo rate, allowed exporters to borrow abroad and continued to reduce three-month treasury bill tenders.
The market has read these signals, and is convinced the authorities are working towards a low rate scenario, they said.
Overnight call money closed at 12.25 percent, with the market well offered, dealers said.
"Money which left the system in December is starting to find its way back," said a Sampath Bank dealer.
